name: Ebed-Melek
title: The Courageous Ethiopian Court Official
summary: Ebed-Melek was an Ethiopian court official (eunuch) who served under King Zedekiah in Jerusalem. He showed extraordinary courage by going against the king's advisors and rescuing the prophet Jeremiah from a cistern where he had been left to die. As a reward for his faith and compassion, he received God's promise of protection during the fall of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Hearing About Jeremiah's Fate
keyEvents.description: Ebed-Melek learned that the officials had thrown the prophet Jeremiah into a mud-filled cistern belonging to Malkijah, the king's son, where he sank in the mud and was in danger of dying.

keyEvents.title: Appealing to the King
keyEvents.description: With great courage, Ebed-Melek went directly to King Zedekiah at the Benjamin Gate and declared that the officials had acted wickedly toward Jeremiah. He argued that the prophet would die of hunger in the cistern.

keyEvents.title: Granted Permission to Rescue Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: King Zedekiah listened to Ebed-Melek and gave him authority along with thirty men to pull Jeremiah out of the cistern before he died.

keyEvents.title: Rescuing Jeremiah with Care
keyEvents.description: Ebed-Melek fetched old rags and cloths from the treasury and lowered them down to Jeremiah with ropes, so that he could place them under his arms to protect himself from the ropes. Then they carefully pulled him up.

keyEvents.title: Receiving God's Promise of Protection
keyEvents.description: Through Jeremiah, God gave a special promise to Ebed-Melek: because he had put his trust in the Lord, he would be spared and survive the fall of Jerusalem. His life would be given to him as plunder.
